title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 43-44
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 43 to 44 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'रामो विरामो विरतो मार्गो नेयो नयोऽनयः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 43 to 44 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 43 to 44.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 43 to 44** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **रामो विरामो विरतो मार्गो नेयो नयोऽनयः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**रामो विरामो विरतो मार्गो नेयो नयोऽनयः । वीरः शक्तिमतां श्रेष्ठो धर्मो धर्मविदुत्तमः ॥** **वैकुण्ठः पुरुषः प्राणः प्राणदः प्रणवः पृथुः । हिरण्यगर्भः शत्रुघ्नो व्याप्तो वायुरधोक्षजः ॥**

He is Rama, the one who gives rest, free of attachment, the guide who leads us on. Without injustice, the greatest hero among the strong, is that God of gods. He is dharma, and the best among those who know dharma. Lord of Vaikuntha, the Supreme Person, life itself is he. The giver of life, the sacred Om, the vast one, is that God of gods. Hiranyagarbha, destroyer of foes, all-pervading, the wind, beyond the senses.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 43 to 44 mean?
faq.a: He is Rama, the one who gives rest, free of attachment, the guide who leads us on. Without injustice, the greatest hero among the strong, is that God of gods. He is dharma, and the best among those who know dharma. Lord of Vaikuntha, the Supreme Person, life itself is he. The giver of life, the sacred Om, the vast one, is that God of gods. Hiranyagarbha, destroyer of foes, all-pervading, the wind, beyond the senses.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
